purpose: Test whether PROTEI_DPI and RDP.RU EcoDPI/EcoFilter/TSPU share code, hardware, ownership, integrators, control-plane components or other causal bridges. Distinguish product identity from ecosystem convergence.

chronology.finding: PROTEI publicly demonstrated PROTEI DPI as a new independent product for deep packet analysis and traffic management.
chronology.implication: PROTEI DPI predates the 2019 sovereign-Runet/TSPU rollout and has its own product history.

chronology.finding: PROTEI deployed its DPI platform commercially at MegaCom in Kyrgyzstan.
chronology.implication: Independent foreign carrier deployment existed years before TSPU.

chronology.finding: PROTEI integrated Entensys/UserGate Web Filter with its DPI at MegaCom; the external product classified requested sites and PROTEI DPI applied policy.
chronology.implication: PROTEI historically used modular third-party classification integrations rather than evidence of RDP code reuse.

chronology.finding: Rostelecom invested 15% in RDP.RU in 2016; PROTEI_DPI entered the Russian software registry in 2017 as its own product (registry no. 3672).
chronology.implication: Separate ownership and software-registration lineages are visible before TSPU.

chronology.finding: RDP.RU and NTC PROTEI were listed as separate candidate vendors in FSB/Roskomnadzor/Mincomsvyaz testing of traffic-filtering systems for Telegram blocking. PROTEI co-owner Anton Pinchuk confirmed the testing context and said PROTEI withdrew; later reporting identified RDP.RU equipment as the most effective in the laboratory experiment.
chronology.implication: This is the strongest anti-rebrand evidence: regulators treated them as distinct competing systems in the selection process that preceded sovereign-Runet/TSPU deployment.

chronology.finding: Sovereign-Runet trials on Russian operator networks publicly identified RDP.RU DPI equipment as the tested system.
chronology.implication: The publicly traceable path into TSPU runs through RDP.RU, not PROTEI.

chronology.finding: Rostelecom group consolidated control of RDP.RU; by 2025 the group stated that 100% of RDP.RU had been collected under its Gradient structure as an intragroup optimization.
chronology.implication: RDP.RU became a controlled Rostelecom-group asset.

chronology.finding: Rostelecom and NTC PROTEI created joint venture PROTEI-RTK for Russian 5G development.
chronology.implication: PROTEI entered a separate formal Rostelecom partnership years after the TSPU vendor-selection period. This is ecosystem convergence, not evidence that older PROTEI DPI became TSPU.

chronology.finding: A current telecom solution presentation lists RDP.RU network-packet-broker functionality and PROTEI PCRF in the same mobile-core architecture as distinct functions.
chronology.implication: They can coexist in one stack as separate components, further weakening a simple label-swap model.

PROTEI_DPI.historic_os: RedHat/CentOS in older public technical description
PROTEI_DPI.current_packet_io: 10G NIC with DPDK support; up to 100G interfaces

RDP_EcoDPI_EcoFilter.current_hardware_line: EcoFilter 5340R family; public reporting also ties current TSPU supply to RDP software on Yadro Vegman server platforms
RDP_EcoDPI_EcoFilter.architecture_style: EcoSGE firmware/software family with separate DU/cEMS/LB/DC roles

software_fingerprint_comparison.comparison_result: Namespaces, package naming, technical-specification prefixes, product modularization and registry identities are visibly different. No public binary/package/config-schema evidence found that one is a relabeled build of the other.

functional_overlap.interpretation: These are normal overlapping capabilities for carrier-grade DPI products and do not establish common code or manufacturer identity.

common_component_check.x86: Both product families can run on commodity/server-class x86 platforms; this is generic and has no attribution value.
common_component_check.DPDK: PROTEI current certification explicitly names DPDK-capable NICs. Public evidence sufficient to make DPDK a PROTEI component exists; no unique DPDK-derived bridge to RDP was established in this pass. Even if both use DPDK, DPDK is widely used open-source packet-processing infrastructure and would carry near-zero identity weight.
common_component_check.database: PROTEI current certificate names ClickHouse. RDP/TSPU ecosystem reporting also contains ClickHouse in monitoring/control infrastructure, but this is generic analytics infrastructure and does not imply a shared DPI codebase.
common_component_check.hardware: PROTEI certification specifies generic minimum server characteristics; RDP/TSPU public evidence points to EcoFilter appliances/Yadro server platforms in modern deployments. No same-appliance/OEM identity was established.
common_component_check.signature_engine: No common proprietary signature database, file format, update endpoint or signature identifier was found.
common_component_check.management_protocol: No common proprietary management API, command namespace, controller hostname, certificate chain or remote-management backend was found.

corporate_and_institutional_links.rostelecom_rdp: Rostelecom invested in RDP.RU in 2016 and consolidated control in 2020; by 2025 100% was held inside Rostelecom group via Gradient.
corporate_and_institutional_links.rostelecom_protei: Rostelecom and NTC PROTEI formed PROTEI-RTK in January 2024 for 5G development.
corporate_and_institutional_links.industry_committee: Both NTC PROTEI and RDP.RU are members of the ARPP Domestic Software telecommunications committee.
corporate_and_institutional_links.coexistence: 2026 mobile-network architecture materials show RDP.RU and PROTEI functions in the same stack as separate named components.
corporate_and_institutional_links.interpretation: A shared institutional ecosystem is confirmed. This can facilitate interoperability, standards alignment, personnel/vendor familiarity or future component reuse, but it is not evidence of product identity.

strongest_negative_evidence_against_rebr: PROTEI DPI was publicly demonstrated in 2012 and commercially deployed abroad in 2014, before TSPU selection/deployment.
In 2018 regulators tested RDP.RU and PROTEI as separate candidate systems; PROTEI withdrew while RDP reportedly performed best.
2019 sovereign-Runet/TSPU trials publicly identify RDP.RU equipment.
PROTEI and RDP have distinct software namespaces, registry entries, technical-spec prefixes and management/component families.
Modern telecom materials can place RDP and PROTEI products side-by-side as separate network functions.

remaining_open_connections.hypothesis: Shared low-level packet-processing libraries beyond generic DPDK
remaining_open_connections.killer_test: Obtain legal/public binaries, SBOMs, package manifests or symbol/version strings and compare proprietary libraries.
Compare update endpoints, feed formats, category IDs, rule identifiers and signature versioning.

remaining_open_connections.hypothesis: Shared OEM or bypass/NIC hardware supplier
remaining_open_connections.killer_test: Compare BOMs, PCI IDs, bypass cards, firmware vendor strings and certification annexes.

remaining_open_connections.hypothesis: Shared management/control-plane code introduced after Rostelecom ecosystem convergence
remaining_open_connections.killer_test: Compare current management APIs, controllers, certificates, telemetry schemas and orchestration components in Rostelecom-integrated deployments.

remaining_open_connections.hypothesis: PROTEI technology used as a non-DPI component inside a broader TSPU site
remaining_open_connections.killer_test: Find procurement/BOM/site documentation naming PROTEI alongside RDP/DCOA components at a TSPU node.

cuba_implication.rule: PROTEI presence in Cuba cannot be translated into TSPU presence.
cuba_implication.still_valid: PROTEI_DPI is technically capable of active filtering and PROTEI has a documented Cuban telecom relationship.
cuba_implication.missing_bridge: Evidence that ETECSA's measured RST/filtering appliance is specifically PROTEI_DPI remains absent.
cuba_implication.new_spider_angle: If Cuban packet behavior can be matched to a known PROTEI deployment such as MegaCom, that would support PROTEI attribution without invoking TSPU identity.

claim_ceiling.allowed: PROTEI and RDP.RU are separate DPI vendors that became increasingly connected through the broader Rostelecom/Russian telecom ecosystem. Their products overlap functionally and may use generic common infrastructure, but no public evidence found shows that PROTEI_DPI is EcoDPI/TSPU under another label.
forbidden_without_new_evidence: PROTEI_DPI and EcoDPI share a proprietary codebase
Cuban PROTEI equipment is a TSPU node
Rostelecom partnership proves shared remote control
shared x86/DPDK/ClickHouse implies common manufacturer or control plane

next_spider_pass: Mine archived PROTEI and RDP manuals for proprietary config-key, API-route, service-name and telemetry-schema overlap.
Search procurement/BOM documents for sites where PROTEI and RDP equipment coexist, especially Rostelecom and DCOA deployments.
Compare public certificates/SBOM-like metadata for NIC vendor IDs, bypass cards, cryptographic libraries and service dependencies.
Use known PROTEI deployment MegaCom as a fingerprint control: locate censorship/middlebox measurements on that network and compare TCP reset behavior with Cuba and RDP/TSPU.
Preserve the distinction between ecosystem relationship and causal product identity.
